result.topic_en: Abel's theorem for the p everywhere-finite integrals $w_\nu=\int\varphi_\nu(s,z)\,dz/(\partial F/\partial s)$ on $F(s,z)=0$, used to integrate the system of p differential equations between p+1 pairs $(s_\mu,z_\mu)$, with a rational function $1/\vartheta$ built from integrals t and w with zero periods.

methods.what: Sum over the n sheets of the derivatives of an everywhere-finite integral is a single-valued function vanishing at infinity to second order, hence identically zero (basis of Abel's theorem)
methods.quote: so ist $\frac{\partial w^{(1)}}{\partial z}+\dots+\frac{\partial w^{(n)}}{\partial z}$

methods.what: Definition of the p everywhere-finite Abelian integrals
System of p differential equations (Abel's theorem in differential form) between p+1 point pairs

General integration of the system by taking the p+1 points as the fibre of a rational function $1/\vartheta$ with simple poles at the initial points, built from integrals t and w with periods made to vanish
